DATE
Monday, Feb. 9, 2026 at 8:30 a.m. ET
CALL PARTICIPANTS
Chief Executive Officer — Gal Krubiner
President — Sanjiv Das
Chief Financial Officer — Evangelos Perros
Head of Investor Relations — Josh Fagen
TAKEAWAYS
GAAP Net Income
-- $34 million for the quarter, marking a fourth consecutive profitable quarter.
Operating Cash Flow
-- $80 million for the quarter, supporting ongoing liquidity improvements.
Full-Year Revenue
-- $1.3 billion, representing a 26% increase year over year.
Adjusted EBITDA
-- $371 million for 2025, up 76% with full-year margin expansion to 28.5%.
Full-Year GAAP Net Income
-- $81 million, a $483 million turnaround from 2024's loss, with EPS of $0.93.
Q4 Revenue
-- $335 million, a 20% year-over-year growth.
Fee Revenue
-- $321 million in the quarter, comprising 96% of total revenue and up 16% year over year.
FRLPC (Fee Revenue Less Production Costs)
-- $131 million for Q4, showing a 12% increase year over year and a 4.9% margin of network volume.
Network Volume
-- $2.7 billion in Q4, up 3% year over year, with personal loans accounting for 65% of total and growing 10%; auto and point of sale representing 19% and 16% respectively; SFR volume was zero (limiting total growth).
Q4 Production Adjustment
-- Late quarter pullback reduced volumes by $100 million to $150 million without impacting quarterly profitability.
Capital Markets Execution Fees
-- Negative $6 million for Q4 and negative $21 million for the year, driven by risk retention cash contributions in ABS structures.
ABS Revolving Capacity
-- Nearly $3 billion across point of sale and personal loans, resulting from recent transactions and providing greater funding visibility.
Cash and Investments
-- Quarter-end cash of $288 million (up $62 million year over year) and $945 million in investments, loans, and securities.
New Investments in Loans and Securities
-- $271 million in Q4, offset by $170 million in capital returned from prior deals.
Corporate Notes Repurchases
-- $7 million repurchased during the quarter at a 12.5% discount to par, with a further $7 million repurchased post-quarter.
Outlook for 2026 (Full Year Guidance)
-- Network volume of $11.25-$13 billion; total revenue of $1.4-$1.575 billion; adjusted EBITDA of $410-$460 million; GAAP net income of $100-$150 million.
Outlook for Q1 2026
-- Network volume of $2.5-$2.7 billion; total revenue of $315-$335 million; adjusted EBITDA of $80-$95 million; GAAP net income of $15-$35 million.
Forward Credit-Related Impairments Guidance
-- $100-$150 million for 2026, consistent with 2025 guidance and reflecting proactive risk management.
Partner Expansion
-- Three new significant partners onboarded: Achieve GLS, a leading buy now pay later provider, and LendingClub's adoption of the affiliate-optimized and prescreen product suite.
Risk Strategy Adjustment
-- Pulled back on higher-risk, less profitable credit segments late in the quarter despite no observed deterioration in consumer performance.
New Forward Flow Agreements
-- Expanded into all three asset classes with Castlelake (auto, personal loans) and SoundPoint Capital (point of sale).
ABS Issuance
-- $2 billion issued in Q4 over seven transactions; recent $800 million ABS deal was upsized from $600 million and oversubscribed.
Operating Expenses
-- Core operating expenses declined to 36% of FRLPC, a 13% improvement year over year.
Partner Pipeline Strength
-- Onboarding pipeline at highest levels in company history, with expectations to add up to eight new partners by end of Q2.
2025 Credit Performance
-- Personal loan cumulative net losses (CNLs) 30%-40% better than 2021 peaks; auto CNLs 50%-70% better than 2022 vintages; point of sale credit trends stable and within expectations.
Tax Rate Assumption
-- Guidance implies a 20% GAAP tax rate for 2026, acknowledging variability as profitability continues to ramp.

RISKS
CFO Evangelos Perros stated, "guidance continues to reflect $100 to $150 million of rolling twelve-month forward credit-related impairments," emphasizing persistent macro and credit uncertainty as a rationale for ongoing caution.
Late-quarter production adjustment proactively reduced Q4 network volume by $100 million to $150 million, with management characterizing this as a response to "increased uncertainty rather than observed deterioration."
Guidance for both Q1 and full-year 2026 explicitly assumes that current uncertainty and reduced volume run rates will persist, potentially leading to "consumer and performance deterioration" if not reversed.
Capital markets execution fees were negative $6 million in Q4 and negative $21 million for 2025 as a direct result of upfront risk retention and more conservative capital market structures.
SUMMARY
Pagaya Technologies

(
PGY

6.95%
)
reported substantial profitability improvement, delivering four consecutive quarters of GAAP net income and significantly strengthening liquidity during the period. Management emphasized deliberate risk reduction in late Q4, shifting away from higher-risk and less profitable credit exposures, and instead prioritizing new partner onboarding and diversified product offerings. Funding stability advanced through expanded ABS programs, increased revolving capacity, and broader forward flow agreements. Outlook for 2026 is shaped by ongoing macro uncertainty, with measured volume and revenue growth guidance that anticipates continued conservative risk positioning. Credit performance across all major asset classes remains within targeted ranges, underpinned by proactive portfolio management rather than reaction to realized losses.
CFO Evangelos Perros said, "We are exiting the year with $10.8 billion of fourth quarter annualized volume. Deliberately shrinking high-risk volume by $1.5 billion on an annualized basis while still delivering year-over-year volume growth."
President Sanjiv Das said, "Existing partners continue to actively adopt our products. In fact, our largest existing partners signed definitive term sheets and adopted the direct marketing engine after a series of tests. And are now scaling with us across direct mail and email prescreen campaigns."
CEO Gal Krubiner said, "we don't see a deterioration, so nothing on the CNL or the CPR," clarifying that portfolio tightening was preemptive and based on forward-looking risk signals, not lagging performance metrics.
Of fees from capital markets execution, Perros explained these "were a negative $6 million for the quarter and a negative $21 million for the year, reflecting the pricing agreements with our forward flow partners and the risk-adjusted pricing of our ABS transactions."
CFO Perros highlighted that late-quarter volume cuts had "no real impact in the long term of the business," framing current optimization as temporary and offset by pipeline growth and new partner contributions.
INDUSTRY GLOSSARY
FRLPC
: Fee Revenue Less Production Costs, a proprietary Pagaya metric reflecting net fee revenue derived after associated production costs, used to assess core profitability per originated or managed asset.
CNL
: Cumulative Net Losses, a credit metric tracking total realized loan losses over the life of an asset or vintage as a percentage of original balance.
ABS
: Asset-Backed Securities, securitized pools of loans or receivables issued to investors as tradeable debt instruments.
Forward Flow Agreement
: A contractual arrangement in which assets (e.g., loans) are sold or funded by an investor on a recurring, forward-looking basis, often used for funding newly originated loans off-balance sheet.
B2B2C
: Business-to-Business-to-Consumer, a model in which a company enables other businesses to serve end-user consumers, in Pagaya’s case via lending partners and product integrations.
